changes_made.explanation: Normalized 'Other:Text-to-SQL' to just 'Text-to-SQL' since it's a valid NLG task. Kept 'Code Generation' as this paper specifically generates SQL code from natural language.
Consolidated all variants to 'Execution Accuracy' as they all refer to the same SQL execution correctness metric. Removed redundant entries and normalized capitalization.
No LLM-as-judge evaluation is conducted. Claude-3-Sonnet is only used for synthetic data generation, not for post-generation evaluation.
No human evaluation conducted - paper relies solely on automatic execution accuracy metrics.

overall_notes: This paper proposes YORO, a text-to-SQL system that internalizes database knowledge. It clearly addresses NLG (SQL code generation) and uses execution accuracy as the automatic evaluation metric. No LLM-as-judge or human evaluation is conducted. The extraction was generally accurate, with minor normalization needed for consistency.
